- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 30-day forecasts start above 80, while true values often dip below 80).
- Overshoots occur after sharp spikes in history (e.g., after 80+ values, model jumps higher than true outcome).
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term — prices often stay elevated longer than they should.
- Forecasts show increasing bias toward higher values as the 30-day window progresses, suggesting model is not adjusting for recent downward trends.
- Model underestimates volatility in the middle-to-late part of the 30-day window, especially after a spike (e.g., 88+ values followed by 80–85).
- Model does not adjust for sudden drops in true values — e.g., after 88+ peaks, model continues rising instead of correcting downward.
- Forecasts are too smooth — fail to reflect sharp, non-linear corrections in true outcomes.
- Model tends to ignore recent low values in history when forecasting — e.g., if history includes 75–77, model still forecasts 80+.
- Model overreacts to recent high values — forecasts rise too aggressively after a spike, then fail to correct.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent low values — e.g., if history includes 70–75, model still forecasts 80+.
- Model does not account for seasonal or event-driven corrections — e.g., after 88+ peaks, model fails to anticipate sharp drops.
- Model is not sensitive to the 30-day moving average — often forecasts above or below the actual 30-day MA, but not aligned with it.
- Model does not adjust for the “tail” of the distribution — e.g., if true values show a sharp drop at the end, model continues rising.
- Model is not responsive to recent volatility — e.g., if true values show high variance, model still forecasts a flat trend.
- Model fails to capture the “reversion to mean” after spikes — e.g., after 90+ values, model continues rising instead of correcting.
- Model does not account for “reversal” after a spike — e.g., if true values drop after a peak, model continues rising.
- Model is not sensitive to “recent low” — e.g., if history includes 70–75, model still forecasts 80+.
